items.q: Revenue rose by 10% to £231m. What was revenue before the rise?
items.why: £231m is 110% of the original. Original = £231m ÷ 1.1 = £210m. Taking 10% off £231m gives the wrong answer, because the 10% was worked out on the smaller original figure.
items.label: New question

items.q: Revenue £10m, Cost of sales £3m, Other expenses £4m, Tax £1m. Gross profit = ?
items.why: Gross profit = Revenue - Cost of Sales = 10 - 3 = £7m. Same principle tested again. Only deduct CoS for gross profit.

items.q: Based on the network, if activity B is delayed by 6 days, the duration of the critical path
items.why: B would take 8 days. Path B–C–E–G then takes 8 + 2 + 8 + 4 = 22 days, against 17 now. The other paths through B are shorter (B–F–H = 18, B–D–G = 16), so the project takes 5 days longer. B had 1 day of float, so only 5 of the 6 days are added.

items.q: Based on the network, what is the total float time for activity D?
items.why: Activity D runs from node 2 (earliest start 2) to node 5 (latest finish 13) and takes 4 days. Total float = 13 – 4 – 2 = 7 days.

items.q: Revenue £61m, cost of sales £21m, operating expenses £15m, net finance costs £1m, taxation £3m. What is the gross profit?
items.why: Gross profit = revenue – cost of sales = £61m – £21m = £40m.
items.label: New question

items.q: In a decision tree there are four possible outcomes of an action. The probabilities of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd outcomes are 0.4, 0.32 and 0.24 respectively. The probability of the 4th outcome is:
items.why: All probabilities at a chance node must sum to 1.0. So: 0.4 + 0.32 + 0.24 = 0.96. The 4th outcome = 1.0 – 0.96 = 0.04. Take your time with the addition: 0.4 + 0.32 = 0.72. Then 0.72 + 0.24 = 0.96.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business sells 12,500 units at £12 each. Variable cost is £10 per unit and fixed costs are £14,000. What is its profit?
items.why: Total contribution = (£12 – £10) × 12,500 = £25,000. Profit = total contribution – fixed costs = £25,000 – £14,000 = £11,000.
items.label: New question

items.q: A factory has 26 employees, each paid £80 a day. It produces 130 units a day and sells each for £10. What are employee costs as a percentage of turnover?
items.why: Each day: employee costs = 26 × £80 = £2,080; turnover = 130 × £10 = £1,300. Employee costs as % of turnover = £2,080 ÷ £1,300 × 100 = 160%.
items.label: New question

items.q: Fixed costs are £36,000 a month and variable costs are £5 per unit. The business makes 7,500 units a month. What is its average (unit) cost?
items.why: Total costs = £36,000 + (£5 × 7,500) = £73,500. Unit cost = total costs ÷ output = £73,500 ÷ 7,500 = £9.80.
items.label: New question

items.q: A factory can produce 8,500 units a month. It produced 6,550 units last month. What is its capacity utilisation?
items.why: Capacity utilisation = actual output ÷ maximum possible output × 100 = 6,550 ÷ 8,500 × 100 = 77.1%.
items.label: New question
